newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU finance ministers approve German plan-source.
newsitem.headline: EU finance ministers approve German plan-source.

text.p: European Union finance ministers on Monday approved Germany's economic convergence plan, aimed at bringing its economy into line for the start of European monetary union.
"They have aproved the plan. There was only a short discussion," a delegation source said.
Under the terms of the plan, Germany intends to cut its deficit to 2.9 percent of gross domestic product this year, down from 3.8 percent in 1996.

That would come in just below the strict target of three percent set in the Maastricht Treaty, which lays down the economic conditions countries must meet this year if they wish to join the single currency in 1999.
Unexpectedly high unemployment at the start of this year has led some independent economists to question whether this goal is achievable.
Germany and France are seen as essential founder members of the single currency.
France's convergence plan was also approved.
